key_insight: Random train/test splits overestimate perovskite ML performance because duplicate recipes leak across splits; provenance-grouped evaluation reveals a truer test of generalisation.
engineering_relevance: For device optimization, the study provides a stricter benchmarking protocol that better distinguishes memorization from physically useful prediction when screening perovskite solar-cell recipes.
method: Mapped institutional provenance in the Perovskite Database.
Built a hierarchy of grouped splits that isolate duplicates, publications, and institutions.
Benchmarked 13 models across random and progressively stricter evaluation settings.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that nearly two-thirds of curated devices share an exact recipe match, making random splits prone to leakage and inflated accuracy.
watch_item: Performance rankings can shift sharply under grouped splits, so models should not be selected using random-split results alone.
paper_title: Provenance-grouped protocol for evaluating machine learning in perovskite photovoltaics
